newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital market closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital market closing report.

text.p: French bond futures followed Bunds and U.S. Treasuries higher late on Thursday to settle at a new contract high but traders said there were no major players behind the move and the contract could slip back on Friday.

The December contract broke through the previous high of 127.62 as Bunds climbed past their previous high at 100.85 to settle 127.66. The French contract reached 127.74, seen as a resistance point, in GLOBEX trading soon after the Matif close.
One futures trader said the move had been driven mainly by local traders looking to see if stops would be triggered above 127.62 but failed to set off any large buy orders.
"Everytime we set a new high fear sets in and I think we could fall back tomorrow," the trader said. "I'm not convinced" by the move above 127.62.
Another trader said rises in the U.S. and German bond markets had driven the French market, following a decline, albeit largely expected, in U.S. real earnings in October.
"We're following Bunds and the U.S., it's just market noise. There's nothing major and there are no big players behind it," the futures trader said.
Traders said, however, there had been hefty buying of the spread between the December and March bond contracts.
Technical analysts said the main objectives for the contract, if the rally continued, would be 127.74, 127.82 and then 128.00. The contract was trading little changed at 127.66 on GLOBEX at 1600 GMT.
Ten-year French government bonds managed to keep pace with their German counterparts. The spread, using the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT, remained steady at parity.

The short end of the curve, however, managed to reverse some the underperformance seen so far this week. The two-year spread narrowed three basis points but was still some way off the low for the year.
The 10-year yield fell as low as 5.82, the lowest level since February 3, 1994.
The Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.20 percent after its monetary policy council meeting as most economists had expected.
Steady French monetary policy did not prevent December PIBOR from posting a small gain, although resistance at 96.47 ensured the contract remained stuck in a narrow range.
Analysts said they still expected the intervention rate to be trimmed by at least five basis points before the end of the year and this hope was supporting the contract.

French welfare debt repayment fund CADES managed to sell another 1.3 billion francs of its three French franc bonds, taking the total sold to 11.281 billion, above its original target amount of eight to 10 billion francs.
As was the case at Wednesday's auction the 2002 bond and 2007 bonds attracted most interest.
The franc continued to fluctuate around 3.38 per mark without making any significant move as the dollar received heavy verbal backing from central bankers and politicians alike.
The French unit was at 3.3792 per mark compared with 3.3795 late on Wednesday.
